name: dsh-modpack-kit
description: Bundle several plugins into one .dshpack and install them in one pass: full packs carry the payloads, lite packs record names and versions and fetch them from the registry, and both ship a standalone installer so a machine with nothing but a bare DSH can install (payloads are copied under ~/.dsh/dsh-modpack/vendor and registered, so deleting the unpacked folder is safe; installed plugins are skipped unless you pass --replace). Each plugin can be packed as upstream-basic or as your local copy. Packing always runs an in-memory scan for secrets and risky code (masked, never written to disk); high-risk hits pause the job until you confirm, then the same job resumes from the scan checkpoint without scanning again, and the confirmation is recorded in the manifest. Installing shares the progress dock: plugins already present are skipped first, then you choose finish-as-is or replace with the packed version; when the market catalog has the same name and you are online, the market version is preferred (switchable). Integrity, compatibility and licences are re-checked, the packed config is re-applied, and install-without-enabling or enable-right-away are both available. Packs can be opened via a file picker, a folder picker, any directory, an imported-packs list (several at once, each showing its packed name, author and description) or an https link. Categories, search, sorting and entries come from the same plugin-market catalog (first screen lists only what you have, paged on the server), and the UI can be shown in settings, the sidebar or the plugins tab, each switchable. Installing the plugin market (dshmarket) first is recommended but not required.
author: Vesna-Strivozha-cn
